sentences.zh: 他们是人口中相当大的一部分。

sentences.en: And the story goes that Ptolemy II sends to Jerusalem for people who can translate the Hebrew scriptures into Greek.
sentences.zh: 故事是说托勒密二世派人去耶路撒冷寻找能将希伯来经文翻译成希腊语的人。

sentences.en: And he has sent 72 scholars, six from each of the 12 tribes of Israel.
sentences.zh: 他派出了72名学者，以色列12个支派每支派6人。

sentences.en: And they are put up on the Pharos, the island with the lighthouse.
sentences.zh: 他们被安置在法罗斯岛，也就是有灯塔的那个岛上。

sentences.en: And they come up with a Greek translation for the Royal Library.
sentences.zh: 他们为皇家图书馆提供了一个希腊语译本。

sentences.en: And this is the Septuagint, the translation of Hebrew scripture into Greek.
sentences.zh: 这就是《七十士译本》，即希伯来经文的希腊语译本。

sentences.en: Septuagint comes from the Latin for 70.
sentences.zh: “Septuagint”一词源自拉丁语中的70。

sentences.en: So, it's a rounding down from the 72.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是从72向下取整的结果。

sentences.en: But this is, as I say, it's a myth.
sentences.zh: 但正如我所说，这是一个神话。

sentences.en: It's contained in a letter supposedly written by a guy called Aristaius in the second century BC.
sentences.zh: 它包含在一封据称由一个叫阿里斯提亚斯的人在公元前二世纪写的信中。

sentences.en: So, long after it's meant to have happened.
sentences.zh: 所以，这距离事情发生的时间已经很久了。

sentences.en: And essentially, it's making a case for the Jews to be a part of Hellenic culture in Alexandria.
sentences.zh: 本质上，这是在为犹太人成为亚历山大希腊文化的一部分寻找理由。

sentences.en: There's chronic antisemitism in Alexandria.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大存在长期的反犹主义。

sentences.en: He's making a pitch to the Greeks to say, look, our learning is a part of the universal corpus of human knowledge.
sentences.zh: 他是在向希腊人推销，说，看，我们的学问是人类知识普遍体系的一部分。

sentences.en: The Ptolemies are interested in it.
sentences.zh: 托勒密王朝对此很感兴趣。

sentences.en: It's gone into the museum, into the library.
sentences.zh: 它进入了博物馆，进入了图书馆。

sentences.en: But the intention of that is very palpable.
sentences.zh: 但其意图是非常明显的。

sentences.en: But one more counter-argument.
sentences.zh: 但还有一个反驳观点。

sentences.en: This is an unusual position because you're very much the revisionist here.
sentences.zh: 这是一个不同寻常的立场，因为你在这里非常像个修正主义者。

sentences.en: And I'm sticking up for the orthodox interpretation of the kind of the library.
sentences.zh: 而我是在坚持对图书馆的那种正统解释。

sentences.en: The more romantic one, I would say, Tom, which is usually you're the more romantic presenter.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，那是一种更浪漫的解释，而你通常是那位更浪漫的主持人。

sentences.en: The rest is history.
sentences.zh: 剩下的就是历史了。

sentences.en: But so, Cleopatra, we're told, I think, by Plutarch that Cleopatra spoke Greek, Egyptian, Ethiopian, Aramaic, Syriac, Median, Parthian, an Arabic language,
sentences.zh: 但是，关于克利奥帕特拉，我想普鲁塔克告诉我们，克利奥帕特拉会说希腊语、埃及语、埃塞俄比亚语、阿拉米语、叙利亚语、米底语、帕提亚语、一种阿拉伯语，

sentences.en: and the language of the Troglodytes.
sentences.zh: 还有穴居人的语言。

sentences.en: Doesn't that speak to a kind of universalism and multiculturalism at the heart of the...
sentences.zh: 这难道不能说明在……的核心存在一种普遍主义和多元文化主义吗？

sentences.en: Because presumably if she did speak any of these languages, she would have learned at least some of them from the scholars working in the museon and the library.
sentences.zh: 因为据推测，如果她确实会说这些语言中的任何一种，她至少会从在博物馆和图书馆工作的学者那里学到一些。

sentences.en: No, because Cleopatra is famously the first of the Ptolemies to speak Egyptian.
sentences.zh: 不，因为克利奥帕特拉是著名的第一位会说埃及语的托勒密统治者。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But maybe that's because Egyptian is regarded as a lower level than some of the others.
sentences.zh: 但也许那是因为埃及语被认为比其他一些语言地位更低。

sentences.en: It doesn't mean that there isn't a kind of great swirl of language.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着不存在一种伟大的语言交融。

sentences.en: I mean...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是……

sentences.en: Well, I think by our lights, it's astounding that the Ptolemies, over all these generations that they've been ruling Egypt, don't learn to speak Egyptian.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我认为以我们的眼光来看，托勒密王朝在统治埃及的这么多代人里，竟然没有学会说埃及语，这令人震惊。

sentences.en: But Timon of Fleas, you had in the first half, in the land of Egypt, where they jabber in a whole range of languages, he said.
sentences.zh: 但你在上半场提到的弗利斯的提蒙曾说，在埃及这片土地上，他们用各种语言叽叽喳喳。

sentences.en: So there is a kind of multiculturalism there in the line.
sentences.zh: 所以那句话里确实有一种多元文化主义。

sentences.en: There must be.
sentences.zh: 一定有的。

sentences.en: No, because he's dismissing it.
sentences.zh: 不，因为他是在贬低它。

sentences.en: He's saying it's not even Greek.
sentences.zh: 他说那甚至不是希腊语。

sentences.en: Most of the people in Egypt speak some barbarous language.
sentences.zh: 埃及的大多数人说的是某种野蛮的语言。

sentences.en: I mean, that's what barbarian is.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是“野蛮人”的意思。

sentences.en: It's someone who doesn't speak Greek.
sentences.zh: 就是指那些不会说希腊语的人。

sentences.en: It goes, bah, bah, bah, bah, bah.
sentences.zh: 听起来就像，吧，吧，吧，吧，吧。

sentences.en: But isn't the implication there that some of the...
sentences.zh: 但那里的暗示难道不是说一些……

sentences.en: He's talking about the scholars specifically, that some of the scholars, that maybe they are all speaking Greek,
sentences.zh: 他专门谈论的是学者们，也许他们都在说希腊语，

sentences.en: but they're coming from different places and there is a kind of exchange.
sentences.zh: 但他们来自不同的地方，确实存在一种交流。

sentences.en: Yeah, but they're all Greek speaking.
sentences.zh: 是的，但他们都说希腊语。

sentences.en: They're only interested in Greek.
sentences.zh: 他们只对希腊语感兴趣。

sentences.en: They're not interested in anything else.
sentences.zh: 他们对其他任何东西都不感兴趣。

sentences.en: Okay, well...
sentences.zh: 好吧，那么……

sentences.en: I think.
sentences.zh: 我想是这样。

sentences.en: We will, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我们会，是的。

sentences.en: Which, to our way of thinking, can't possibly equate to universal, but to the Greeks, it does.
sentences.zh: 这在我们看来，绝不可能等同于普遍，但对希腊人来说，确实如此。

sentences.en: For instance, you will note that Cleopatra isn't speaking Latin, which is amazing, considering that her two boyfriends are both Roman.
sentences.zh: 例如，你会注意到克利奥帕特拉不会说拉丁语，这很神奇，考虑到她的两个男朋友都是罗马人。

sentences.en: How did she speak to them, Tom?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，她是怎么和他们交流的？

sentences.en: Did they both speak Greek?
sentences.zh: 他们都会说希腊语吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because there is assumption that Greek is the only language that you need.
sentences.zh: 因为人们认为希腊语是你唯一需要的语言。

sentences.en: Well, I suppose that's the thing, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想这就是关键所在，不是吗？

sentences.en: That Greek is perceived as being the language of learning and of culture across the Mediterranean in this period.
sentences.zh: 即希腊语在这一时期被视为整个地中海地区的学习和文化语言。

sentences.en: Yeah, so basically, I think that the Library of Alexander isn't nearly as universal as people think.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以基本上，我认为亚历山大图书馆并不像人们想象的那样普遍。

sentences.en: So that essentially is one myth.
sentences.zh: 所以这本质上是一个神话。

sentences.en: The other great question is, what happens to it?
sentences.zh: 另一个大问题是，它发生了什么？

sentences.en: Where does it go?
sentences.zh: 它去哪儿了？

sentences.en: And that is usually framed as, who destroys it?
sentences.zh: 这通常被表述为，是谁摧毁了它？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The assumption is that someone or some kind of great sweeping catastrophe of fire has wiped the library out.
sentences.zh: 人们的假设是，某个人或某种巨大的火灾灾难摧毁了图书馆。

sentences.en: So a favourite candidate, as you'll know, Dominic, because you write about it in your book on Cleopatra, is Julius Caesar.
sentences.zh: 所以，多米尼克，正如你所知，因为你在关于克利奥帕特拉的书中写过，一个热门的嫌疑人是尤利乌斯·凯撒。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Are you convinced by that?
sentences.zh: 你对此深信不疑吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Caesar causes a fire.
sentences.zh: 凯撒确实引发了一场火灾。

sentences.en: There's no doubt about that.
sentences.zh: 这一点毫无疑问。

sentences.en: When he's trapped in Alexandria, having visited Egypt as part of his war against Pompey, he's installed himself.
sentences.zh: 当他被困在亚历山大港时，作为他与庞培战争的一部分，他访问了埃及，并驻扎在那里。

sentences.en: He's taken possession of the palace quarter.
sentences.zh: 他占领了宫殿区。

sentences.en: He ends up being shacked up with Cleopatra.
sentences.zh: 他最终和克利奥帕特拉住在一起。

sentences.en: He's fighting against her brother, isn't he, Ptolemy?
sentences.zh: 他在和她的兄弟托勒密作战，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Of course, they're all called Ptolemy.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们都叫托勒密。

sentences.en: And in the course of this, there is a big fight down at the harbour.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，港口发生了一场大战。

sentences.en: Caesar, it seems, if you're to believe the accounts, sets fire to his own ships to stop the enemy getting hold of them.
sentences.zh: 据记载，凯撒似乎为了阻止敌人占领，放火烧毁了自己的船只。

sentences.en: And in the course of that, the fire spreads from the ships to the warehouses, and the books there are damaged.
sentences.zh: 火势从船只蔓延到仓库，那里的书籍因此受损。

sentences.en: But I mean, as you will know, Tom, the library is not at the docks.
sentences.zh: 但汤姆，你应该知道，图书馆并不在码头。

sentences.en: So it's conceivable that the fire spread, but it would have had to have spread a hell of a long way.
sentences.zh: 所以火势蔓延是可以想象的，但它必须蔓延很长一段距离才行。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: What do you think about it?
sentences.zh: 你怎么看？

sentences.en: Well, so the confusion is caused by Plutarch, who does say the library is destroyed in this fire.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这种困惑是由普鲁塔克引起的，他确实说图书馆是在这场火灾中被毁的。

sentences.en: And we don't quite know where he gets that.
sentences.zh: 我们不太清楚他是从哪儿得来的消息。

sentences.en: Well, we do know where he gets it from, because it's evident that large quantities of books were destroyed.
sentences.zh: 其实我们知道他从哪儿得来的，因为很明显有大量的书籍被毁了。

sentences.en: And this is recorded in a number of sources, all of which seem to go back to Livy,
sentences.zh: 这在许多资料中都有记载，而这些资料似乎都追溯到李维，

sentences.en: who is the great Roman historian who's writing shortly after the lifetime of Julius Caesar in the reign of Augustus.
sentences.zh: 也就是那位伟大的罗马历史学家，他在奥古斯都统治时期，即凯撒去世后不久撰写了这些记录。

sentences.en: And he says that there are warehouses that contain grain and books.
sentences.zh: 他说当时有存放谷物和书籍的仓库。

sentences.en: Another detail that seems to derive from Livy is that 40,000 scrolls were stored there by chance.
sentences.zh: 另一个似乎源自李维的细节是，当时恰好有四万卷卷轴存放在那里。

sentences.en: So that, by chance, is crucial, because it's saying they're not there as part of a permanent collection.
sentences.zh: 所以“恰好”这个词很关键，因为它说明这些书并不是作为永久收藏的一部分存放在那里的。

sentences.en: They happen to be there.
sentences.zh: 它们只是碰巧在那里。

sentences.en: And why would they happen to be there?
sentences.zh: 那它们为什么会碰巧在那里呢？

sentences.en: Well, we talked earlier about this great trade in books, taking books, taking scrolls to Rome and to Italy and to the great plutocrats of the Roman world.
sentences.zh: 我们之前谈到过当时盛大的图书贸易，将书籍和卷轴运往罗马、意大利以及罗马世界的那些大富豪手中。

sentences.en: And probably that's what this is.
sentences.zh: 这很可能就是原因所在。

sentences.en: Well, you said yourself, Egypt is a great exporter of papyrus.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你自己也说过，埃及是莎草纸的主要出口国。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: And I think we have pretty conclusive proof that the library, whatever it was, whether it was part of the museum or whether it was something separate,
sentences.zh: 我认为我们有相当确凿的证据表明，无论图书馆是什么，它是博物馆的一部分还是独立的机构，

sentences.en: was still in existence in the reign of Domitian, who is end of the first century AD, because Suetonius,
sentences.zh: 在图密善统治时期，也就是公元一世纪末，它依然存在，因为苏维托尼乌斯，

sentences.en: he's describing a fire that sweeps Rome in Domitian's reign and how Domitian sends scribes to Alexandria to make copies of the texts that have been lost in the libraries in Rome.
sentences.zh: 他描述了图密善统治时期席卷罗马的一场大火，以及图密善如何派遣抄写员前往亚历山大港，复制在罗马图书馆中丢失的文本。

sentences.en: So there's this sense that Alexandria remains the great depository of texts where you would go.
sentences.zh: 所以人们认为亚历山大港依然是那个你可以去寻找文本的伟大宝库。

sentences.en: So then the question, well, if not Julius Caesar, then when?
sentences.zh: 那么问题来了，如果不是凯撒，那是什么时候？

sentences.en: And the fact is that over the course of the third century and into the fourth, when the Roman world is ravaged by civil war and all kinds of catastrophes,
sentences.zh: 事实是，在三世纪到四世纪期间，当罗马世界饱受内战和各种灾难蹂躏时，

sentences.en: there are any number of disasters that might have destroyed the museum and the library.
sentences.zh: 有无数场灾难可能摧毁了博物馆和图书馆。

sentences.en: So there's a great cycle of destruction under Caracalla at the beginning of the third century, Aurelian,
sentences.zh: 三世纪初卡拉卡拉统治下有一场巨大的破坏，还有奥勒良，

sentences.en: who is the emperor who kind of stitches the empire back together after it seems to be disintegrating in the mid third century.
sentences.zh: 他是在三世纪中期帝国似乎即将瓦解时，将其重新拼凑起来的皇帝。

sentences.en: And it's specified that the Bruchaeon, which is the area with all the palace, that Aurelian had destroyed it.
sentences.zh: 据明确记载，布鲁基昂区，也就是宫殿所在的区域，被奥勒良摧毁了。

sentences.en: So if he's destroyed the palace, then he must have destroyed the museum as well.
sentences.zh: 所以如果他摧毁了宫殿，那他也一定摧毁了博物馆。

sentences.en: And then we're told that there was another cycle of destruction in the reign of Diocletian at the end of the third century.
sentences.zh: 然后我们得知在三世纪末戴克里先统治时期又发生了一轮破坏。

sentences.en: So I would say that the odds on anything remaining of it by the end of the fourth century would be minimal.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，到四世纪末，它还能剩下什么的几率微乎其微。

sentences.en: Not least because, Tom, Alexandria is not just a city of tremendous sophistication and culture and so on, but it is notorious as a city of mob violence, of rioting.
sentences.zh: 尤其是因为，汤姆，亚历山大港不仅是一座拥有极高文明和文化的城市，而且以暴民暴力和骚乱而闻名。

sentences.en: The Alexandrians are famously given to civic disorder and they're always burning down bits of their city, smashing things up.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大人以热衷于社会动乱而著称，他们总是烧毁城市的一部分，打砸东西。

sentences.en: So it's hard to imagine that in that intervening period of time, from the end of the Ptolemies all the way through to the fourth century,
sentences.zh: 所以很难想象，在从托勒密王朝末期一直到四世纪的那段漫长时期里，

sentences.en: that the library would have survived utterly unscathed, given that they're always having these ruckuses and riots.
sentences.zh: 考虑到他们总是发生骚乱，图书馆能毫发无损地幸存下来。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Except that the most famous example of mob violence actually happens in 391.
sentences.zh: 但最著名的暴民暴力事件实际上发生在391年。

sentences.en: So that is almost a century after Constantine's conversion to Christianity.
sentences.zh: 那是在君士坦丁皈依基督教近一个世纪之后。

sentences.en: And it is when a Christian mob turns on the great temple of Serapis,
sentences.zh: 当时一群基督徒暴徒袭击了伟大的塞拉皮斯神庙，

sentences.en: who is this syncretic artificial deity who'd basically been invented by the Ptolemies to try and provide a focus for both their Greek and Egyptian subjects.
sentences.zh: 塞拉皮斯是托勒密王朝为了凝聚希腊和埃及臣民而发明的一种融合性的人造神祇。

sentences.en: But this is a very vast, impressive building.
sentences.zh: 这是一座非常宏伟、令人印象深刻的建筑。

sentences.en: Anyone who's seen the film Agora with Rachel Weisz is the centerpiece of that.
sentences.zh: 看过蕾切尔·薇兹主演的电影《城市广场》的人都知道，那是电影的核心场景。

sentences.en: It's brilliantly well done.
sentences.zh: 拍得非常出色。

sentences.en: And the theory is that there was a library in there that this was either a part of or a subdivision or a rival to the main library of Alexandria,
sentences.zh: 有一种理论认为，里面有一个图书馆，它是亚历山大主图书馆的一部分、分支或竞争对手，

sentences.en: and that this Christian mob attacked the Serapium and destroy it and deliberately target the library.
sentences.zh: 而这群基督徒暴徒袭击了塞拉皮斯神庙并将其摧毁，还蓄意针对图书馆。

sentences.en: Now, this is a myth that emerges basically in the writings of Edward Gibbon, the author of The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire, who has, I mean,
sentences.zh: 这其实是一个主要出现在《罗马帝国衰亡史》作者爱德华·吉本著作中的神话，他，我是说，

sentences.en: he has his own reasons to present Christians as bigots.
sentences.zh: 他有自己的理由将基督徒描绘成偏执狂。

sentences.en: And they're the villains of his book.
sentences.zh: 他们是他书中的反派。

sentences.en: So he writes, the valuable library of Alexandria was pillaged or destroyed, and near 20 years afterwards,
sentences.zh: 所以他写道，亚历山大港珍贵的图书馆被洗劫或摧毁，近20年后，

sentences.en: the appearance of the empty shelves excited the regret and indignation of every spectator whose mind was not totally darkened by religious prejudice.
sentences.zh: 空荡荡的书架让每一位未被宗教偏见完全蒙蔽的旁观者感到遗憾和愤慨。

sentences.en: So the idea that the books would be destroyed, but the shelves left, I mean, it's obviously, Gibbon is thinking of the shelves of the Bodleian being stripped, I think, there.
sentences.zh: 所以这种认为书被毁了但书架还在的观点，我想吉本当时想到的应该是博德利图书馆被清空的情景。

sentences.en: And that is an idea that is immensely popular today among writers.
sentences.zh: 这种观点在今天的作家中非常流行。

sentences.en: I think of it, for example, of the few years ago, the book The Darkening Age by Catherine Nixie, where she basically argued,
sentences.zh: 比如几年前凯瑟琳·尼克西写的《黑暗时代》，她基本上认为，

sentences.en: all this tremendous learning of the classical world was destroyed by the Christians, that Christianity was responsible for plunging the world into a darkening age, as she calls it.
sentences.zh: 古典世界所有伟大的知识都被基督徒摧毁了，基督教导致世界陷入了她所说的“黑暗时代”。

sentences.en: On that, we have five accounts of the destruction of the Serapeum.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，我们有五份关于塞拉皮斯神庙被毁的记录。

sentences.en: So it is one of the best authenticated episodes in the whole history of Alexandria, but none of them mention the destruction of a library.
sentences.zh: 所以这是亚历山大港整个历史上最确凿的事件之一，但没有一份记录提到图书馆被毁。

sentences.en: And to the degree that classical texts have survived, it's down to the efforts of Christian copyists, Christian scribes.
sentences.zh: 古典文本之所以能流传至今，全靠基督徒抄写员和文士的努力。

sentences.en: Without them, we would have nothing.
sentences.zh: 没有他们，我们将一无所有。

sentences.en: So I don't think the Christians did it, and I definitely don't think the Muslims did it, but they also have been fingered as culprits.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为不是基督徒干的，也绝对不是穆斯林干的，尽管他们也被指为罪魁祸首。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's lots of stuff on the internet saying that they're the bad guys in the story.
sentences.zh: 是的，网上有很多说法称他们是故事里的坏人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So this is even more improbable.
sentences.zh: 所以这更加不可信。

sentences.en: But the story is that the Arabs sweep into Egypt.
sentences.zh: 但故事是这样的：阿拉伯人席卷埃及。

sentences.en: They conquer it.
sentences.zh: 他们征服了它。

sentences.en: They lay siege to Alexandria.
sentences.zh: 他们围攻亚历山大港。

sentences.en: They capture it.
sentences.zh: 他们占领了它。

sentences.en: The commander of the Arabs, Amar, writes to Omar, the caliph, and says, well, you've got all this great city.
sentences.zh: 阿拉伯指挥官阿慕尔写信给哈里发欧麦尔说，你拥有了这座伟大的城市。

sentences.en: There's this enormous library.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个巨大的图书馆。

sentences.en: It's full of books.
sentences.zh: 里面全是书。

sentences.en: What should we do with them?
sentences.zh: 我们该怎么处理它们？

sentences.en: And he waits, and then Omar's reply comes back.
sentences.zh: 他等待着，然后欧麦尔的回信来了。

sentences.en: If the content of the books you mention is in accordance with the book of Allah, we may do without them, for in that case, the book of Allah more than suffices.
sentences.zh: 如果这些书的内容符合真主的经典，那我们就不需要它们了，因为真主的经典已经足够了。

sentences.en: If, on the other hand, they contain matter not in accordance with the book of Allah, there can be no need to preserve them.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，如果它们包含的内容不符合真主的经典，那也没有保留它们的必要。

sentences.en: Proceed then and destroy them.
sentences.zh: 那就去毁掉它们吧。

sentences.en: We have no need of other books.
sentences.zh: 我们不需要其他的书。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, it's so clearly not true.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这显然不是真的。

sentences.en: This is not, again, the Muslims had huge respect for the legacy of Greek philosophy.
sentences.zh: 这不对，穆斯林对希腊哲学的遗产有着极大的尊重。

sentences.en: The reason that this survives is that it's kind of in accordance with what people who are very hostile to institutional religion like to imagine about it.
sentences.zh: 这个故事之所以流传下来，是因为它符合那些非常敌视制度化宗教的人对宗教的想象。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: You know, it's all bigots who have no time for anything other than their own holy books.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就是那种除了自己的圣书之外什么都容不下的偏执狂。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's a kind of enlightenment myth, really.
sentences.zh: 这其实是一种启蒙运动的神话。

sentences.en: So do you think the idea that there was one single moment when the library is destroyed is simply a product of the 18th century?
sentences.zh: 那么你认为“图书馆在某一时刻被摧毁”的观点，仅仅是18世纪的产物吗？

sentences.en: A fantasy, a projection, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我想这是一种幻想，一种投射。

sentences.en: And that actually what happened was that the library probably fell partly into disuse.
sentences.zh: 实际上，图书馆可能只是部分被废弃了。

sentences.en: Bits of it were perhaps burned in fires.
sentences.zh: 其中的一部分可能在火灾中被烧毁了。

sentences.en: Who knows?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that actually just the collection was split up.
sentences.zh: 实际上，藏书只是被分散了。

sentences.en: And who knows?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: It wasn't even an event, actually, but a slow process that nobody even noticed.
sentences.zh: 这甚至不是一个事件，而是一个没人注意到的缓慢过程。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think the idea of there being a dark age, you want to think, well, why was there a dark age?
sentences.zh: 我认为关于“黑暗时代”的观点，你会想，为什么会有黑暗时代？

sentences.en: And it's much more dramatic if you can blame it, say, on the destruction by fire of a single vast repository of learning.
sentences.zh: 如果你能把它归咎于一场大火摧毁了单一的巨大知识宝库，那会戏剧性得多。

sentences.en: But actually, you know, right at the beginning of this episode, we talked about how, unlike clay tablets, which survive when they're fired, papyrus is incredibly fragile.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，你知道，在这一集的开头，我们谈到了与火烧后能保存下来的泥板不同，莎草纸极其脆弱。

sentences.en: You don't actually need a fire to destroy it.
sentences.zh: 你其实根本不需要火来摧毁它。

sentences.en: But if you're keeping all these scrolls in, you know, they're not air conditioned, they're not temperature checked, they're a mice, they crumble away.
sentences.zh: 如果你把这些卷轴存放在那里，没有空调，没有温度控制，还有老鼠，它们就会碎掉。

sentences.en: They crumble when you're reading them.
sentences.zh: 它们在你阅读时就会碎掉。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Unless those texts are being rewritten and rewritten and rewritten, they're going to fall away.
sentences.zh: 除非这些文本被不断地重抄，否则它们终将消失。

sentences.en: I mean, it may be that, I mean, we're told that the buildings of the palace complex are destroyed by Aurelian.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，也许，我们被告知宫殿建筑群是被奥勒良摧毁的。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe that is the final terminus for it.
sentences.zh: 也许那是它的最终终点。

sentences.en: But I suspect that most of the texts had already gone long, long before that.
sentences.zh: 但我怀疑大部分文本在那之前很久很久就已经消失了。

sentences.en: And actually, the person who comments most wonderfully on this is Gibbon, who, as well as being an enthusiast for kind of various enlightenment-enthused myths, is a brilliant,
sentences.zh: 实际上，对此评论得最精彩的人是吉本，他不仅是各种启蒙运动神话的热衷者，也是一位杰出的、

sentences.en: brilliant scholar who has studied and investigated all the available sources for the narratives that he's telling.
sentences.zh: 博学的学者，他研究并调查了他所讲述的叙事的所有可用来源。

sentences.en: And he writes that, I sincerely regret the more valuable libraries which have been involved in the ruin of the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 他写道：我真诚地为那些在罗马帝国废墟中消失的珍贵图书馆感到遗憾。

sentences.en: But when I seriously compute the lapse of ages, the waste of ignorance, and the calamities of war, our treasures, rather than our losses, are the object of my surprise.
sentences.zh: 但当我认真计算岁月的流逝、无知的浪费和战争的灾难时，我感到惊讶的不是我们失去的，而是我们保留下来的宝藏。

sentences.en: So don't mourn what we've lost, but celebrate what we've retained.
sentences.zh: 所以不要哀悼我们失去的，而要庆祝我们保留下来的。

sentences.en: I mean, that's actually quite a nice message, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这其实是一个很好的信息，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Very un-Gibbonian, given that he's normally so sceptical and so sort of...
sentences.zh: 这很不“吉本”，考虑到他平时总是那么怀疑，那么……

sentences.en: Well, no, I think, you know, the decline and fall is a great monument to the amount of texts that are there.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不，我认为《衰亡史》本身就是现存文本的一座伟大丰碑。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I guess that Gibbon is, you know, that's what he is expressing.
sentences.zh: 我想吉本表达的就是这个意思。

sentences.en: Thank God I don't have to do any more reading.
sentences.zh: 谢天谢地，我不用再读书了。

sentences.en: That's what he's thinking.
sentences.zh: 他心里想的就是这个。

sentences.en: But to repeat, you know, again, what we said at the beginning,
sentences.zh: 但重申一下，正如我们开头所说的，

sentences.en: I think the fact that the Library of Alexander is no longer there is precisely what gives it its potency as a kind of mythic symbol of libraries.
sentences.zh: 我认为亚历山大图书馆不复存在的事实，恰恰赋予了它作为图书馆神话象征的力量。

sentences.en: What a wonderful story, Tom.
sentences.zh: 多精彩的故事啊，汤姆。

sentences.en: I really enjoyed that.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢。

sentences.en: And actually, that's fired me up for two things.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这激发了我对两件事的兴趣。

sentences.en: One is the city of Alexandria would be a fantastic story, actually, to do, and the rest is history, the rise and fall of Alexandria.
sentences.zh: 一是亚历山大城本身就是一个很棒的故事，亚历山大的兴衰史。

sentences.en: But also the Ptolemies, the Ptolemaic dynasty, the Hellenistic world.
sentences.zh: 还有托勒密王朝，托勒密家族，希腊化世界。

sentences.en: We haven't really done much about them.
sentences.zh: 我们还没怎么讲过他们。

sentences.en: We did Cleopatra, but I love the story of the Ptolemies.
sentences.zh: 我们讲过克利奥帕特拉，但我喜欢托勒密家族的故事。

sentences.en: It's very complicated because they're always marrying each other, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 这很复杂，因为他们总是近亲结婚，不是吗？

sentences.en: And they're all called Ptolemy.
sentences.zh: 而且他们都叫托勒密。

sentences.en: And they're all called Ptolemy, which might be an issue.
sentences.zh: 他们都叫托勒密，这可能有点问题。

sentences.en: But they have amusing nicknames, which we could...
sentences.zh: 但他们有有趣的绰号，我们可以……

sentences.en: Yeah, there's Son of the Eighth, Fatty.
sentences.zh: 是的，有“八世之子”、“胖子”。

sentences.en: Yeah, Ptolemy, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，托勒密，没错。

sentences.en: He married his sister and his niece at the same time.
sentences.zh: 他同时娶了自己的妹妹和侄女。

sentences.en: Great stuff.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Fantastic behaviour.
sentences.zh: 精彩的行为。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: On that bombshell, thank you so much for that, Tom.
sentences.zh: 带着这个重磅消息，非常感谢你，汤姆。

sentences.en: That was really good fun.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: And do you want to plug your library again?
sentences.zh: 你想再宣传一下你的图书馆吗？

sentences.en: British Library, yes.
sentences.zh: 大英图书馆，是的。

sentences.en: It's 50th birthday.
sentences.zh: 它50岁生日了。

sentences.en: All kinds of exhibitions and specials on at the library.
sentences.zh: 图书馆里有各种展览和特别活动。

sentences.en: So if you're in London and have a chance to go and sample them, please do.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在伦敦，有机会去尝尝的话，请一定要去。

sentences.en: And hurrah for libraries, basically.
sentences.zh: 总之，为图书馆欢呼吧。

sentences.en: Because without them, we wouldn't be able to do this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 因为没有它们，我们就没法做这个播客了。

sentences.en: No, no, especially the Bodleian Library.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错，尤其是博德利图书馆。

sentences.en: Right, we'll see you all next time, everybody.
sentences.zh: 好了，各位，我们下次再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
